pageCache.pageTitle: Forest View Primary School - Values and Ethos
pageCache.text:
Values and Ethos
Statement of Values and Ethos
Children at the heart of every decision
At Forest View, we put children at the heart of every decision we make.
We believe that every child is unique, capable and deserving of the opportunity to succeed. We value each individual within our school community, celebrate their achievements and encourage them to recognise what they can achieve through effort, curiosity and determination.
Our expectations are high because we believe in our children. We want them to enjoy coming to school, to be proud of what they achieve and to develop the knowledge, skills, confidence and character they need for the future.
Above all, we want every child to become a Forest Venturer and to:
Try. Learn. Lead the Way.
These three words capture what we want for every child at Forest View.
Try means having the confidence and courage to take on new experiences and challenges, even when success is not guaranteed.
Learn means being curious, working hard, thinking deeply and understanding that mistakes and challenges are an important part of becoming better.
Lead the Way means developing the confidence, independence and character to make positive choices, set a good example and make a difference to others.
We want our children to understand that learning is a gift and that, with the right opportunities, encouragement and support, everyone has the right to succeed.
What we want for our children
Working in partnership with parents, carers and our wider community, we want every child at Forest View to:
become confident and increasingly independent learners;
Excellence and opportunity for everyone
We are ambitious for our children and for the community we serve.
We want to ensure that a child's circumstances never limit their aspirations or opportunities. Our aim is not simply for children to make progress while they are at Forest View, but for them to develop the knowledge, confidence and ambition that will allow them to make choices about their own futures.
We recognise that children do not all learn in the same way or start from the same point. Through high-quality teaching, appropriate adaptation, support and challenge, we work to ensure that every child can access learning, experience success and make strong progress.
Our curriculum is shaped by the children and community we serve while providing the breadth, ambition and knowledge children need to understand the wider world. We combine high academic expectations with engaging learning and rich experiences that encourage children to ask questions, explore ideas and discover their individual strengths.
Our values
At the heart of Forest View are two core values:
Kindness and Resilience
We believe these provide strong foundations for learning and for life.
Kindness helps children understand the importance of their words and actions, value others, build positive relationships and contribute to their community.
Resilience gives children the confidence to persevere when something is difficult, learn from setbacks, adapt to challenges and keep moving forward.
Alongside kindness and resilience, we explicitly promote and celebrate:
Honesty • Tolerance • Cooperation • Invention • Courage
These values are not simply words displayed around our school. We want children to understand them, recognise them and demonstrate them through their actions. They are strengthened through our curriculum, assemblies, relationships, expectations and the many opportunities children have to contribute to school life.
Preparing children for life beyond Forest View
Our values sit alongside the fundamental British values of democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty, mutual respect and tolerance of those with different faiths and beliefs.
Through their everyday experiences at Forest View, children learn to listen to others, respect different viewpoints, understand rights and responsibilities, make positive choices and contribute to the communities of which they are part.
Ultimately, we want every child to leave Forest View as a successful learner and a confident, responsible young person who is well prepared for the next stage of their education.
We want them to leave knowing that they can face new challenges, learn from their experiences, show kindness towards others and have the confidence to make a positive difference.
We want every child to leave Forest View ready to Try, Learn and Lead the Way.

pageCache.pageTitle: Forest View Primary School - Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND)
pageCache.text:
Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND)
Every child belongs at Forest View
At Forest View, children are at the heart of every decision we make. We are ambitious for every child and believe that a child's starting point, background or additional needs should never place a limit on what we believe they can achieve.
We are proud to be an inclusive school. Children with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND) are supported to learn alongside their peers, access an ambitious curriculum and participate fully in the wider life of the school.
Our approach reflects our values of kindness and resilience and our ambition for every child to become a Forest Venturer: to Try, Learn and Lead the Way. Your current SEND Policy makes this same commitment through ambitious expectations, inclusive practice, removing barriers and enabling children with SEND to access the curriculum alongside their peers.
Our approach to SEND
All teachers at Forest View are responsible for the progress and development of children with SEND. High-quality, inclusive teaching is our first response when a child is experiencing difficulty.
We recognise that children have different strengths, starting points and needs. Teachers set high expectations and adapt their teaching to enable children to access ambitious learning. Where a child requires support that is additional to or different from that ordinarily available, we work with the child and their family to understand their needs and decide what provision is appropriate.
We follow the graduated approach:
Assess • Plan • Do • Review
This helps us understand a child's strengths and barriers, plan appropriate support, put that support into place and evaluate the difference it makes. Provision is then adapted as our understanding of the child develops.
Working with families
We believe that parents and carers are essential partners in supporting children with SEND.
If you have concerns about your child's learning, development, communication, wellbeing or progress, please speak to their class teacher in the first instance. The class teacher can then involve our Assistant Headteacher (Inclusion) where appropriate. This reflects the process established within your current policy and Information Report.
Where children receive SEND support, families are involved in agreeing outcomes and reviewing progress. Children's views are also sought in a way appropriate to their age and communication needs.
Inclusion beyond the classroom
Inclusion at Forest View is about much more than accessing lessons.
We want children with SEND to participate fully in the entire Forest View experience, including educational visits, enrichment, sport, performances, outdoor learning, clubs, leadership opportunities and community activities.
Where necessary, we make reasonable adjustments and provide appropriate support so that children can participate safely and successfully. Your current SEND arrangements explicitly support children with SEND to engage in school activities alongside their peers.
A child's background, circumstances or additional needs should not determine the experiences available to them.
Supporting wellbeing and belonging
We want every child to feel safe, valued and that they belong at Forest View.
Some children may require additional support with communication, emotional regulation, relationships, confidence, sensory needs or mental health. Support is matched to individual need and may include adaptations to everyday teaching, targeted support from appropriately trained staff or involvement from external professionals.
When appropriate, the school works with specialist services including Educational Psychology, Speech and Language Therapy, Occupational Therapy, the Advisory Teaching Service, Early Help and relevant health professionals.
Who should I contact about SEND?
Our SEND provision is coordinated by:
Gemma Lyons Assistant Headteacher (Inclusion) Email: glyons@forestview.gloucs.sch.uk Telephone: 01594 822241
If you have a concern about your child, we recommend speaking to their class teacher first. They can work with you and involve the Assistant Headteacher (Inclusion) as appropriate.

Curriculum
Please click on the links below to find an overview of the school's curriculum. If you would like to find out more information about the school's curriculum then please email: admin@forestview.gloucs.sch.uk or contact the school office from our contact us page.
Individual subject information can be found by going to the relevant page on our website (see links on the right hand side)
Individual class overview's can be found by going to the class section of the website.
Our Curriculum
A curriculum designed for Forest View children
At Forest View, children are at the heart of our curriculum.
Our curriculum is ambitious for every child and has been carefully designed to meet the needs of the children and community we serve. It provides children with the knowledge, skills, experiences and opportunities they need to succeed at Forest View, be fully prepared for the next stage of their education and develop the confidence and curiosity to engage with the wider world.
We want every child to become a Forest Venturer and to:
Try. Learn. Lead the Way.
Our curriculum brings this ambition to life. It encourages children to try new things and embrace new experiences, to learn deeply and build knowledge over time and ultimately to lead the way by becoming confident, independent and responsible young people.
Ambition for every child
We have high expectations for every child at Forest View, regardless of their starting point or background.
Our curriculum enables children to:
We recognise that children have different starting points and different needs. High-quality teaching, appropriate adaptation, support and challenge help ensure that all children, including those with SEND and those who may experience disadvantage, are able to access an ambitious curriculum and experience success.
become confident, curious and increasingly independent learners;
develop their individual talents, interests and creativity;
communicate confidently and develop a rich vocabulary;
Rooted in our community, looking out to the world
Our location in the Forest of Dean is an important part of our identity. We want children to understand, appreciate and take pride in the community and environment in which they grow up.
At the same time, we recognise that growing up in a rural community can mean that some children have fewer opportunities to encounter particular places, cultures and experiences beyond their immediate locality.
Our curriculum therefore deliberately broadens children's experiences and horizons.
Through carefully chosen visits, visitors, texts, practical activities and wider opportunities, we help children to experience and understand a world beyond their immediate surroundings. This includes opportunities to explore different environments, places, communities, cultures, beliefs and ways of life.
These experiences are not additions to our curriculum. They are an important part of it. They develop children's vocabulary and background knowledge, provide meaningful contexts for learning, raise aspirations and help children make connections between what they learn in school and the wider world.
We want children to leave Forest View proud of where they come from and confident about where they can go.
Building knowledge from EYFS to Year 6
Our curriculum provides a clear and progressive journey from children's earliest experiences in the Early Years through to the end of Year 6.
In the Early Years, children learn through an ambitious and carefully planned curriculum that builds on what they already know and can do. Communication and language, early reading, personal development and strong foundations in literacy and mathematics are particularly important, alongside rich opportunities to explore, create, investigate and understand the world.
As children move through the school, their knowledge and skills are deliberately developed and built upon. Curriculum planning identifies the important knowledge children need to learn in each subject and ensures that new learning connects with what has been taught before.
Teachers regularly check what children know and understand. Assessment is used purposefully to identify misconceptions, adapt teaching, provide additional support or challenge and determine when children are ready to move their learning forward.
We recognise the particularly important role of language, reading and vocabulary in children's success. The ability to read confidently and communicate effectively gives children access to every area of the curriculum and opens opportunities throughout their lives. Developing these skills is therefore a priority from children's earliest days at Forest View and throughout their time with us.
Bringing learning to life
We want children to remember what they learn, but we also want them to remember what it felt like to learn it.
Where meaningful links can be made, learning is brought together through engaging themes and purposeful contexts. Children experience practical activities, educational visits, visitors and opportunities to apply their knowledge in ways that make learning relevant and memorable.
Our approach combines these rich experiences with carefully sequenced subject knowledge. Each subject has clearly identified learning so that children progressively build the knowledge and skills they need as they move through the school.
Our individual subject pages explain in greater detail what children learn, how learning develops over time and the knowledge and skills we expect children to acquire.
Enrichment: experiences beyond the classroom
At Forest View, we believe that a child's education extends far beyond the National Curriculum. Enrichment is an important part of our curriculum and of what it means to be a Forest Venturer.
Our enrichment offer is designed to broaden horizons, inspire curiosity, raise aspirations and create memorable experiences. We want every child to have opportunities to discover new interests, recognise their strengths and talents, develop their confidence and experience things that may otherwise sit beyond their everyday lives.
Throughout their time at Forest View, children experience a rich programme of educational visits, visitors, performances, sporting opportunities, outdoor learning, leadership roles, community projects and extra-curricular activities. These opportunities complement classroom learning and help children make meaningful connections between what they learn in school and the wider world.
Our enrichment programme provides opportunities across five broad areas:
We deliberately connect enrichment to our curriculum wherever it can deepen children's knowledge and understanding. Experiences are selected because they add value to children's education, introduce them to new possibilities or provide opportunities to apply what they have learned in meaningful contexts.
Enrichment also provides an important opportunity for children to live out our school values of kindness and resilience, alongside honesty, tolerance, cooperation, invention and courage. Through working with others, taking responsibility, performing, competing, creating, exploring and sometimes stepping outside their comfort zones, children develop character as well as knowledge.
Most importantly, we want enrichment to be for every child. A child's background or circumstances should not determine the experiences available to them. We therefore work to ensure that all children can benefit from the wider opportunities that form part of life at Forest View.
Through these experiences, our children learn to Try things they may never have experienced before, Learn about themselves and the world around them, and develop the confidence to Lead the Way.
Values through our curriculum
Our curriculum develops more than academic knowledge.
At its heart are our two core values:
Kindness and Resilience
Alongside these, we promote and celebrate honesty, tolerance, cooperation, invention and courage.
Children experience opportunities to develop these values throughout school life and through the curriculum. We want them to learn how to work successfully with others, listen to different viewpoints, persevere when something is challenging, make thoughtful decisions and understand the impact their choices can have on other people.
Our curriculum also actively promotes the fundamental British values of democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty, mutual respect and tolerance of those with different faiths and beliefs. Children learn about rights and responsibilities, different cultures and communities, and the importance of respecting others.
Together, our curriculum and values prepare children to participate positively in modern Britain and the wider world.
A curriculum that continues to develop
Our curriculum is never regarded as finished.
Leaders and teachers regularly review what is taught and how well children are learning it. We consider children's outcomes, their work, their knowledge and understanding, feedback from pupils and staff, and developments within individual subjects.
We also look beyond Forest View. As part of the Forest of Dean Trust, and through our work with other schools, educational partners, teacher training and research, we learn from others and contribute our own expertise to the wider education community.
Where changes will improve children's learning or opportunities, we adapt and strengthen our curriculum.
The impact of our curriculum
Ultimately, the success of our curriculum is measured by the children who leave Forest View.
We want children to achieve well academically, but our ambitions extend beyond results.
By the end of Year 6, we want our children to have developed secure knowledge, strong foundations in reading, writing and mathematics, curiosity about the world, confidence in themselves and the resilience to respond to challenges.
We want them to recognise their own strengths and talents, respect and value other people and understand that their background should never limit what they can achieve.
Most importantly, we want every child to leave us ready for the opportunities and challenges ahead.
They leave Forest View ready to Try, Learn and Lead the Way.

Admissions and Prospectus
Welcome to Forest View
We are delighted that you are considering Forest View Primary School for your child.
Choosing a school is an important decision, and we warmly encourage prospective families to visit us, meet our staff and children and experience Forest View for themselves.
Forest View Primary School is part of the Forest of Dean Trust. The Trust is the admission authority for the school and the school's admission arrangements are set out in the policies available at the bottom of this page. As an academy trust, the Forest of Dean Trust is required to comply with the statutory School Admissions Code.
If you would like to arrange a visit to Forest View or have any questions about joining the school, please contact the school office. We will be very happy to help.
Starting School in Reception
Children normally start primary school in the September of the school year in which they turn five.
Applications for Reception places are coordinated by Gloucestershire County Council. Parents must therefore apply to the County Council rather than directly to Forest View. An application must be made even if your child already attends a nursery or pre-school connected with a particular school or has an older brother or sister attending the school.
Parents are encouraged to use all of the preferences available to them and list schools in their genuine order of preference. All applications submitted by the closing date are treated equally, regardless of when during the application window they were submitted.
Apply for a Reception place
Applications and full information about the process are available through Gloucestershire County Council School Admissions:
Apply for a Reception school place through Gloucestershire County Council
You can also visit the Council's main School Admissions page for further information and guidance:
Gloucestershire County Council School Admissions
Joining Forest View During the School Year
Applications for children joining Forest View outside the normal Reception admissions round are known as in-year applications.
This may include children who:
In Gloucestershire, in-year applications are made directly to the school. Gloucestershire County Council does not coordinate in-year admissions on behalf of schools.
are transferring from another school; or
How to apply for an in-year place at Forest View
Parents and carers wishing to apply for an in-year place should:
Gloucestershire's current procedure states that schools should notify parents of the outcome of an in-year application within 10 to 15 school days.
In-Year Application Form
Download the Gloucestershire In-Year Admission Application Form
Full guidance about applying for a school place during the school year can be found here:
Gloucestershire County Council: Applying for a school place during the school year
Completed applications can be sent to the school office at:
Forest View Primary School Latimer Road Cinderford Gloucestershire GL14 2QA
Email: admin@forestview.gloucs.sch.uk
What Happens if a Year Group is Full?
Where Forest View has places available, applications will be considered in accordance with the school's published admission arrangements.
Where there are more applications than places available, places must be allocated in accordance with the published oversubscription criteria contained within the relevant Admissions Policy. Academy admission authorities must allocate places according to their published arrangements and oversubscription criteria.
If we are unable to offer your child a place, we will write to you to explain the decision and provide information about your right of appeal. Gloucestershire County Council can also provide advice about other schools that may have places available.
For further advice about in-year admissions, parents can contact Gloucestershire County Council's In-Year Admissions Team:
Telephone: 01452 426015 Email: inyear.admissions@gloucestershire.gov.uk
Admission Appeals
Parents and carers have a statutory right of appeal if their application for a school place is refused.
Admission appeals are heard by an independent appeal panel. The panel is independent of the school and admission authority. Academy admission authorities are required to make parents aware of their right of appeal when refusing admission.
Further information about the appeals process, including how to make an appeal, is available from Gloucestershire County Council:
https://www.gloucestershire.gov.uk/schooladmissions/information-on-admission-appeals/
Admission Outside a Child's Normal Age Group
Parents may request that their child is admitted to a year group outside their normal age group.
Any such request will be considered in accordance with the School Admissions Code and the school's published admission arrangements. Decisions will be made on the circumstances of the individual case and in the child's best interests. The School Admissions Code contains specific provisions relating to children being educated outside their normal age group and deferred entry for children below compulsory school age.
Parents considering making such a request are encouraged to contact the school so that we can discuss their child's individual circumstances.
Children with an Education, Health and Care Plan
The admission arrangements described above are different for children who have an Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP).
Where a school is named in a child's EHCP, admission is dealt with through the statutory EHCP process rather than through the standard admissions procedure. The School Admissions Code requires children whose statutory plan names the school to be admitted.
If your child has an EHCP or you would like to discuss Forest View's provision for children with SEND before applying, please contact our SEND team through the school office.
You can also find further information on our SEND section of the website.
Visiting Forest View
We believe that visiting a school is one of the best ways to decide whether it is right for your child.
We are proud of Forest View and would be delighted to show prospective families around the school. During your visit, you will have an opportunity to see our learning environment, meet members of our team and find out more about our curriculum, values and wider opportunities.
To arrange a visit, please contact the school office.
Our Admissions Policies
The formal admission arrangements and oversubscription criteria for Forest View are contained within the relevant Admissions Policy below.
School Prospectus
You can find out much more about life at Forest View, including our curriculum, school day, uniform, pastoral support and opportunities for children, in our school prospectus which can be found below.

pageCache.text:
Ofsted and Performance
The school's performance table can be viewed at: www.compare-school-performance.service.gov.uk/school
Results for the most recent academic year can be viewed below.
What Ofsted says about Forest View
Forest View Primary School was inspected by Ofsted on 5 and 6 November 2024. The inspection concluded that the school had “taken effective action to maintain the standards identified at the previous inspection.” Forest View had previously been judged Good for overall effectiveness.
We are particularly proud that the inspection report reflects many of the things that we believe make Forest View special.
Ofsted described Forest View as:
Inspectors recognised that the school has high expectations for children's learning and behaviour and noted that this is reflected in their achievements. Most importantly, they recognised that our ethos of "putting children first" is threaded through all that the school does.
Children who enjoy school and are proud to learn
The report describes our pupils as "a credit to the school", recognising them as friendly, polite and caring. Inspectors found that children enjoy school, understand the expectations we have of them and demonstrate consistently positive attitudes towards their learning.
Ofsted also recognised children's enthusiasm for learning, noting that:
The inspection highlighted the strength of early reading and mathematics and recognised that the school has developed an ambitious curriculum in English and mathematics, with strong academic outcomes.
Every child supported to succeed
Inclusion is at the heart of Forest View, and we were particularly pleased that inspectors recognised the school's commitment to enabling all pupils to succeed.
Ofsted found that the school identifies quickly when children require additional help and provides "sharply focused and highly effective pastoral and academic support." Inspectors recognised that this enables all children, including pupils with SEND and children who speak English as an additional language, to access the same curriculum as their peers.
The positive relationships between children and adults were also recognised. Inspectors found that pupils feel valued and cared for and know there is always an adult they can talk to when they are worried.
Strong partnerships with families
Working closely with families is fundamental to the way we work at Forest View.
Ofsted recognised that our pastoral provision is strong and that the school "forges highly effective partnerships with families." Inspectors found that these relationships help us provide families with the support they need.
The report also noted that parents were overwhelmingly positive about the school, with parents typically describing Forest View as a school that:
Experiences that broaden children's horizons
Our commitment to providing children with experiences beyond the classroom was also recognised by Ofsted.
Inspectors highlighted the interesting experiences provided to enhance the curriculum, including educational visits, opportunities to learn about and celebrate different cultures and experiences involving members of our wider community.
The report recognised the contribution the school makes to children's broader development, including opportunities to participate in clubs, sport, music, arts and crafts and activities that encourage children to contribute to and support others within their communities.
This reflects an important part of our ambition for Forest View children: that they leave us proud of where they come from and confident about where they can go.
Keeping children safe
Children told inspectors that they feel safe at Forest View. Ofsted found that staff develop supportive and trusting relationships with pupils and that children are confident adults will help them with any worries or problems.
The inspection concluded that:
Always looking to improve
We are proud of our inspection report, but at Forest View we also believe that strong schools never stand still.
The inspection identified further development needed within some foundation subjects, particularly around identifying precisely the knowledge and skills children need to learn, providing opportunities to revisit learning and strengthening assessment. Ofsted also recognised that the school had already begun adapting this part of the curriculum.
This work forms part of our continued development of the curriculum as we strive to provide the very best education and opportunities for every child.
You can read our November 2024 Ofsted report in full on the school website or directly through Ofsted (https://reports.ofsted.gov.uk/provider/21/139150)

Mental Health Support Teams in Schools | Information for Parents
Forest View Primary School
Schools play an important role in supporting the wellbeing of children and young people at a time when they are experiencing lots of physical, emotional and social changes.
For some children, this stage of growing up can sometimes become overwhelming or difficult to manage, and it can be made worse by life events such as changing schools, exams, challenging home circumstances, bullying or difficult friendships.
New Mental Health Support Teams have been put into over 70 schools across Gloucestershire to tackle these challenges by helping young people to feel more resilient, arming them with techniques to look after themselves and strategies to help them cope better with life’s ups and downs. The teams will also support parents and teachers with information and tips about how best to help children and young people who are experiencing difficulties.
The teams are made up of Education Mental Health Practitioners, Primary Mental Health Workers, TiC+ Counsellors and Team Managers. They will travel to each school for meetings with staff to discuss any children and young people they think may benefit from their support. If a child is refusing to go to school, they will also work with families to help the child get back to school.
When a school notices a child is struggling with day-to-day worries, an initial discussion with the team will take place to ensure this form of support is the most appropriate way forward.
Parents and/or carers will be contacted and asked to agree consent prior to any support being started with their child.
The only reason we may not be able to keep things confidential is if we believe a child, young person or someone else is at serious risk of harm.
If you would like any further information regarding the Mental Health Support Team, please contact either Mr Law-Eadie, Miss Woskett or Mrs Lyons at the school on 01592 822241. Alternatively you can email on MHST@forestview.gloucs.sch.uk

pageCache.pageTitle: Forest View Primary School - About us
pageCache.text:
About us
Welcome to Forest View Primary School
Welcome to Forest View Primary School, a proud member of the Forest of Dean Trust. Situated in the heart of the beautiful Forest of Dean, our school is at the centre of the community we serve.
At Forest View, children come first. This principle sits at the heart of our decision-making and shapes everything we do. We want every child who joins our school to feel happy, safe and valued, while being challenged and supported to achieve their very best.
We are ambitious for all of our children. Our curriculum has been carefully designed to meet the needs of the children and community we serve, combining high expectations and academic excellence with enjoyment, creativity and memorable experiences. We believe children learn best when they are engaged, curious and excited about their learning.
Life at Forest View is about much more than what happens in the classroom. We want our children to experience a rich and varied primary education that helps them discover their talents and interests and develops their confidence. From exciting trips and visits to practical experiences such as cookery, sport, the arts and opportunities to explore the world around them, we work hard to give children experiences they will remember long after they leave us.
Being surrounded by the Forest of Dean gives our school a very special sense of place. We want our children to understand and appreciate their local community while also developing the knowledge, skills and aspirations that will open doors to the wider world.
We are proud of the strong relationships that exist between our children, staff, families and wider community. We recognise that parents and carers know their children best and we value the partnership between home and school. By working together, we can give every child the support, encouragement and opportunities they need to flourish.
Throughout their time with us, we encourage every child to become a Forest Venturer and to live out our simple but powerful motto:
Try. Learn. Lead the Way.
For us, being a Forest Venturer means having the confidence to try something new, the determination to learn from successes and challenges and the character to lead the way through their actions and choices. We want children to leave Forest View not only well prepared for the next stage of their education, but also curious, resilient and confident in what they can achieve.
We are extremely proud of Forest View and of the children and community we serve. Whether you are already part of our school community or are considering Forest View for your child, we hope our website gives you a flavour of what makes our school special.
We warmly invite prospective families to come and visit us, meet our children and staff and see Forest View for themselves.

pageCache.pageTitle: Forest View Primary School - Seesaw and Learning at Home
pageCache.text:
Seesaw and Learning at Home
Children's Seesaw Accounts
Every child has their own Seesaw account, which can be accessed using a unique QR code or alphanumeric code through the Seesaw Class app. The app is available for Android and Apple devices, or Seesaw can be accessed through a web browser at:
https://app.seesaw.me/#/login
Throughout the year, children use Seesaw to build a digital journal of their learning. Teachers can also use the platform to share homework and other learning activities, which children can complete and submit for their teacher to see and respond to.
Learning When Your Child Is Absent
We understand that there will be times when children are unable to attend school.
If your child is absent from school but is well enough to continue with some learning at home, parents can request work through Seesaw. Please contact your child's class teacher on the morning of the absence and they can arrange for appropriate learning to be made available.
There is, of course, no expectation that a child who is unwell should complete school work. Their health and recovery should always come first. This provision is there for children who are unable to attend school but are well enough to engage with learning.
Where a child is absent for a longer period, we will work with families to help them remain connected with their learning wherever this is appropriate.
Seesaw for Parents
Parents can also access Seesaw Family, which allows you to see your children's learning journals in one place.
Once you have used the QR code or alphanumeric code provided by school to activate your account, you can create your own password and login details.
Through Seesaw Family, you can:
See examples of your child's learning
Receive school letters and key school communication
Need Help with Seesaw?
If you have difficulty accessing Seesaw, have lost your login details or need help setting up your account, please speak to your child's class teacher or contact the school office. We will be happy to help.
